newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba welcomes U.S. congressional visitors.
newsitem.headline: Cuba welcomes U.S. congressional visitors.

text.p: Two separate groups of U.S. congressmen are visiting Cuba this week in the first such trips since Cuban fighters shot down two small U.S. planes last February, officials said on Tuesday.

Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina told reporters that Reps. Xavier Becerra and Esteban Torres, both California Democrats, on Monday concluded a fact-finding trip to the island during which they met President Fidel Castro.

Robaina gave no other details of the trip by Torres and Becerra. But he said no special significance should be put on a visit that was fairly normal given Cuba's ongoing ties with political, economic and cultural sectors in the United States -- despite the lack of diplomatic ties between Washington and Havana.

State media said another congressional group, consisting of two current House members -- Republicans Toby Roth of Wisconsin and Jon Christensen of Nebraska -- and eight former members, arrived on Monday in the Cuban capital for a stay of several days.
Their trip was arranged by an association of former members of Congress, and they were expected to meet senior Cuban officials including parliamentary president Ricardo Alarcon.
The plane downings Feb. 24 prompted President Bill Clinton to toughen the longstanding U.S. embargo against Cuba and caused a chill in already frosty relations between the two countries.
Numerous U.S. congressmen have visited Cuba over the years and there were several such visits in January and February this year. These stopped after the plane downings.
